subject: DPA evidence: operational telemetry, subprocessors, and model-improvement carveouts
messages:
From: Aisha Malik <aisha.malik@healthbridge.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@healthbridge.com
Date: Tue, 7 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA: model improvement / telemetry exceptions and evidence request

Hi Stephanie / David,

Thanks for the quick sync yesterday. As we move toward procurement we need two clarifications so our legal and security teams can sign off:

1) No-training / model improvement carveout: HealthBridge requires an explicit contractual commitment that our customer data will not be used to improve public models or internal model training pipelines unless we opt in. Please confirm the language you typically accept and flag any operational limitations.

2) Operational telemetry and logs: we understand platforms need monitoring. We need:
   - A short description of what telemetry Redwood retains (request IDs, prompt text, response text, latency/trace data).
   - Retention windows for each category and a deletion / proof-of-deletion workflow.
   - Which subprocessors will see customer prompts/responses (please provide the subprocessor inventory).

Attached is our redline (HealthBridge_DPA_v2_redline.pdf) with the clauses highlighted. Two specific asks in the redline: require onshore KMS for key material used for tenant-level encryption, and 90-day maximum retention for any raw customer transcripts used for debugging (we can accept operational exceptions for ephemeral traces).

Can you share an evidence pack (subprocessor list, sample audit trail showing deletion, confirmation on training opt-out) and a proposed contract fallback if you cannot meet onshore KMS for a specific subprocessor? We need this by end of week to hit our procurement window.

Appreciate it — let me know if a short 15-min call helps.

Best,
Aisha Malik
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
HealthBridge

Attachments: HealthBridge_DPA_v2_redline.pdf (PDF, 378KB)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Malik <aisha.malik@healthbridge.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Jun 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA: model improvement / telemetry exceptions and evidence request

Aisha — thanks for the clear redline and the timeline. We're on it. High level: Redwood can commit to a no-training contractual clause for your tenant (no customer prompts/responses used to train or improve models) and we have an operational evidence flow to demonstrate that. There are a couple of operational caveats (monitoring/health telemetry) I want to call out below so expectations are aligned.

Owners: David (ops & evidence), Kimberly (legal contracting), Karthik (platform/security) are looped to collect the pack.

Quick clarifying Qs so we prepare the right artifacts:
 - When you say "90 days for raw customer transcripts", do you mean all transcripts including ephemeral session buffers or only persisted transcripts accessible through APIs/export?
 - Is onshore KMS a hard requirement for all keys, or can we scope it to keys used for long-term persisted exports/backups?

Proposed timeline: initial evidence items (subprocessor list + sub-processor roles) by EOD Wednesday; full ops evidence (sample audit trails, deletion steps, proposed contracting language) by Friday EOD. If that works I will route items internally with priority.

On operational caveats: we cannot realistically guarantee zero retention of extremely short-lived internal traces used for distributed tracing (these are not stored alongside customer transcripts and are scrubbed quickly) — we will include that as an operational exception and show auditability and deletion timelines. We can however guarantee no training pipelines consume your data and will include an attestation.

I'll include the original redline and our suggested clause in the Friday package.

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Jun 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA: model improvement / telemetry exceptions and evidence request

Stephanie / team — taking the lead on the ops evidence. Summary checklist below and ETA.

Checklist (we will attach artifacts):
- Subprocessor inventory: full list of subprocessors and roles (see attached subprocessor_inventory.csv). I flagged which subprocessors process customer prompts/responses (three entries: logging/backup service, metrics aggregator, managed infra provider).
- Telemetry categories and retention:
   * Request metadata (request IDs, timestamps, latency): retained 180 days by default for troubleshooting; can be downscoped to 90 on request for a specific account.
   * Raw prompts/responses: persisted only when customers enable exports or when sessions are explicitly stored; default retention is 90 days for persisted transcripts.
   * Traces/spans/distributed traces: ephemeral (max 7 days in internal traces), not associated with customer transcript store.
- Deletion workflows: API-driven deletion + backfill purge job + S3 lifecycle; we will include example audit trail showing a deletion request and subsequent log entries.
- KMS/onshore: we support customer-managed KMS and have an option to use onshore key vault regions for tenant keys. Some subprocessors (managed infra provider) operate in shared regions — for those we propose a contractual carveout where we keep tenant encryption with onshore CMK and limit subprocessors' access to encrypted blobs only.
- Attestation: we can provide a signed attestation that customer data will not be used in model training pipelines and an operational runbook for how we enforce that (access controls, QA gates).

ETA: attach subprocessor_inventory.csv here; compiling the audit proof & attestation — target Fri, 2027-06-11 EOD. If HealthBridge needs the 90-day max as a hard platform-wide default, we should confirm now — otherwise we will prepare the scoped option and proposed contract language.

Attachments: subprocessor_inventory.csv (CSV, 12KB)

-David
David Kim
Director, Platform Security & Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Malik <aisha.malik@healthbridge.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA: model improvement / telemetry exceptions and evidence request

Aisha — attaching the evidence pack we promised and summarizing the key points inline so your legal/security teams can quickly map to the redline.

Summary (high-level):
- No-training commitment: Redwood will accept a tenant-scoped no-training clause. Contract language is included in the attachment ("No-Training-Attestation.txt") and we will sign an operational attestation that we will not use HealthBridge prompts/responses to improve models unless you explicitly opt in.
- Subprocessors: attached subprocessor_inventory.csv lists all subprocessors; three vendors will handle persisted transcripts for backup/analytics. We propose a narrow contractual requirement that those subprocessors are restricted to encrypted blobs unless you require onshore-only processing (see below).
- Telemetry & retention: default retention windows we operate by are: request metadata 180 days (can be reduced to 90 for HealthBridge), persisted transcripts 90 days, traces/spans 7 days. We will implement a 90-day policy for your account for request metadata and persisted transcripts if HealthBridge confirms. We also included an example audit trail showing a deletion request and subsequent purge entries.
- KMS/onshore: we support customer-managed keys and onshore key storage. For any subprocessor that operates outside your required geography, we will ensure tenant data is stored encrypted with your CMK and only give subprocessors access to ciphertext. If HealthBridge requires subprocessors themselves to be onshore, we will flag that as a procurement exception and recommend the contract carveout.

Attachments included in the zip (ops-evidence-summary.zip):
 - subprocessor_inventory.csv
 - example_audit_trail.txt (redacted)
 - No-Training-Attestation.txt
 - proposed_contract_language.docx

Next steps:
1) Please confirm whether HealthBridge will accept: (A) onshore CMK for tenant keys + ciphertext-only access for offshored subprocessors, and (B) a 90-day retention for request metadata and persisted transcripts.
2) If yes, Kimberly will circulate a contract mark with language aligned to our attestation and Karthik/David will support a short call if your tech team wants to walk the evidence.

DocuSign link for minor DPA amendment: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/abc123-deploy

If you prefer a 15-min tech walkthrough, we can do Wed 6/16 or Thu 6/17.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out quickly.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Field Legal & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Attachments: ops-evidence-summary.zip (ZIP, 1.2MB)
